key_insight: Electric-field-driven switching in Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 occurs through cooperative O3c/O4c oxygen exchange with a transient “detour” bond-formation pathway, not simple ionic displacement.
engineering_relevance: Preserving this cooperative oxygen-exchange pathway could guide the design of more durable, scalable ferroelectric memories with stable polarization switching and low macroscopic strain.
method: Electric-field-induced molecular dynamics simulations on a defect-free ideal HZO lattice
Fine-tuned machine-learning force field (MACEField) to model atomic dynamics
Trajectory analysis of oxygen coordination changes, bond formation, and polarization response
evidence_signal: The simulations dynamically reproduced the P–E hysteresis loop and revealed the oxygen-exchange switching pathway, including transient detour behavior and internal self-compensation of local volume changes.
watch_item: The mechanism was demonstrated on an ideal defect-free lattice, so defects, interfaces, and real-device disorder may alter switching pathways and endurance.
paper_title: Transient Detour and Cooperative Oxygen Exchange in the Polarization Switching of Ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2
